correctness.rationale: Exact exhaustive breadth-first enumeration of all \(19\,683\) matrices and all \(236\) idempotent transitions yields minimum-length counts \(236,3068,12953,3308,117\) and stabilizes at width \(5\) with only \(-I_3\) unrepresented. The independently checked length-five predicate is exactly \(A^2=I_3\), \(\operatorname{tr}A=2\), with \(A\) nonscalar. Since \(t^2-1\) is square-free over \(\mathbb F_3\), these matrices are diagonalizable with eigenvalue multiplicities \(1\) and \(2\), hence are exactly the similarity class of \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1)\), whose class size is \(117\).

evidence: Theorem 1.2 gives only general logarithmic bounds for full matrix Jordan algebras; Lemma 2.4 is a padding upper bound; Proposition 4.3 gives a seven-factor bound for cyclic matrices.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These statements guarantee representability and upper/lower bounds but do not force width 5 for order three over the ternary field, do not determine all minimum lengths, and do not identify the extremal class.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper states the same definitions and broad full-matrix theorem but does not determine the exact order-three ternary width. Its exact classification is restricted to order two. Targeted statement-, alias-, parameter-, and implication-level searches found no covering result. The retained risk is an unindexed or differently phrased finite computation.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational note or older small-field calculation may contain an equivalent census under different terminology.
No claim is made about uniqueness of methods or about other finite fields.

source_inspections.assessment: NOT_COVERING: exact elementwise lengths are established for order two, while order three is covered only by general representability and bounds. No ternary order-three census or extremal similarity class is stated.

The full Section 4 inspection gives constructions and bounds, not the present exact finite result.

It replaces a broad interval bound by the exact width, the full minimum-length distribution, and a structural description of the extremal stratum.
